subject: Gen7 PresentationHinge source-age/timebase integrity handoff
body: HEAD revalidated unchanged at 633c75be26001d5a4ef6e04c7696e8246713be44. Independent review of Primary Gen7 Core V1 found a distinct clock/freshness defect: chooseTarget() and FrameTarget.measurementAgeMs use callback-now minus deliveryTimeNs, while prediction horizon uses sourceTimeNs. Current Fold7AngleAuthority permits precise source age up to 192ms, so delayed-but-valid trusted geometry can be classified fully fresh after arrival. Deterministic reproduction on exact V1: source=10ms, delivery=100ms, callback=110ms, expected=118ms => mode=TRACKING, reported age=10ms, true physical source age=100ms, horizon=50ms, confidence=1.0. Two-line research-only correction switches freshness/diagnostic age to sourceTimeNs; same case => BLACKOUT_PREDICT, age=100ms, confidence=0.74418604; original Gen7 stock harness still PASS including 100,000 randomized iterations. This is additive to Manager's sourceTime>deliveryTime validation gap: the reproduced case has valid source<=delivery ordering. Platform revalidation also confirms FrameTimeline expectedPresentationTime is System.nanoTime-domain while SensorEvent.timestamp is elapsedRealtimeNanos-domain; current main already has TransitionClock + TimestampQuality/uncertainty conversion substrate, so Android Gen7 integration should reuse it and not pass raw untyped clock values into the pure model. Recommend Manager independently reproduce, then Primary fold source-age semantics plus explicit canonical-time adapter/typing into revised core. No production writes; CI/physical NOT_RUN.
process_observations: The pure-core package made adversarial reproduction cheap and deterministic; keep this packaging pattern.
The stock fuzz constrained delivery lag to 0-15ms while semantic precise authority tolerates up to 192ms source age, leaving an important cross-layer boundary untested.
Reuse TransitionLab clock provenance/quality infrastructure at the Gen7 adapter rather than creating a second normalization scheme.
